newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai court approves drug suspect extradition to U.S.
newsitem.headline: Thai court approves drug suspect extradition to U.S.

text.p: A Thai criminal court on Monday approved an American request to extradite Li Yung Chung, who is accused of masterminding the biggest heroin haul in U.S. history.

The court said Li, who was sent back to Bangkok from Burma on Saturday after he skipped bail and left Thailand in March, would be kept in the Thai capital for 15 days in case he decided to appeal the decision.

Li, handcuffed and dressed in a beige T-shirt and khaki shorts, said in a calm voice: "I am pleased for the quick justice system in deciding to extradite me and I am confident of my legal defence in the United States."
A prosecution source, who declined to be named, told Reuters Li had told him during questioning that he had spent 20 million baht ($769 million) bribing Thai officials to help him jump bail in March.
But Li, a Thai citizen with ethnic Chinese background, refused to answer reporters when asked if he had paid bribes.
He was indicted by a New York court in May 1996 in connection with a 486 kg (nearly 1,070 lb) heroin haul in Hayward, California, in 1991.
